Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) with a VectorFunctionSpace (P1 Lagrange, vector-valued) for the displacement field and a direct linear solver (e.g., MUMPS/PETSc KLU).
Formulate 2D small-strain linear elasticity under plane-stress conditions with unit thickness, using the reduced plane-stress constitutive law: C = E/(1-ν²) * [[1, ν, 0], [ν, 1, 0], [0, 0, (1-ν)/2]].
Material properties: E = 70e9 Pa, ν = 0.33, ρ = 2700 kg/m³, g = 9.81 m/s².
The domain is a 1 m × 0.5 m rectangular plate in the xy-plane (x ∈ [0,1], y ∈ [0,0.5]) with a circular hole of radius 0.1 m centered at (0.5, 0.25).
The right edge of the plate is modified to include a circular arc of radius 0.02 m centered at (1, 0.25), spanning ±30° (π/6 rad) symmetric about the positive-x direction from the arc center; the arc bulges outward to x = 1.02 at its midpoint.
The remaining portions of the right edge (y < 0.25 − 0.02·sin(π/6) and y > 0.25 + 0.02·sin(π/6)) remain straight at x = 1.
A tangential traction of magnitude t_θ = M / (2π·r) = 800 / (2π·0.02) ≈ 6366.2 Pa is applied on the circular-arc portion of the boundary, directed along the local tangent to the arc (counterclockwise sense: at angle θ from the x-axis the traction vector is (−sin θ, cos θ) · t_θ).
A uniform body force f = (0, −ρ·g) = (0, −26467.5) N/m³ is applied over the entire domain to represent gravity in the −y direction.
Dirichlet boundary condition: u = (0, 0) on the entire left edge (x = 0).
Neumann (natural) boundary condition: the hole boundary and all remaining edges (top, bottom, non-arc right edge) are traction-free.
Generate a triangular mesh with 64 elements per edge of the base 1×0.5 rectangle, refined to conform to the hole and the arc geometry.
Solve the variational problem: find u ∈ V such that ∫ C : ε(u) : ε(v) dx = ∫ f · v dx + ∫ t · v ds for all test functions v ∈ V, with the Dirichlet condition applied via DirichletBC.
Post-process and output: the displacement field u, the in-plane Cauchy stress tensor σ = C : ε(u), and the von Mises stress σ_vm = sqrt(σ_xx² − σ_xx·σ_yy + σ_yy² + 3·σ_xy²), saved as VTK/XDMF files for visualization.
